newsitem.title: USA: GM says metals squeeze hasn't hurt its supply.
newsitem.headline: GM says metals squeeze hasn't hurt its supply.

text.p: A General Motors Corp. spokesman on Friday said an acute shortage of platinum and palladium has not posed a supply problem for the world's largest automaker.

Prices of platinum are at their highest since 1990, while palladium prices are at a 17-year peak because Russia has stopped exports. Both precious metals are used in catalytic converters to filter harmful gases and particles from car and truck exhaust systems.
GM spokesman Thomas Klipstine said the automaker has had a strategy in place for several years to set long-term contracts with a variety of sources that ensure it an adequate supply of the metals.
"We have a number of programs in place so we don't have to worry about the short-term hits," he said.
He declined to discuss specifics of how much GM has on hand or what prices it paid.

On Thursday, the United Auto Workers union set a strike deadline of midnight June 12 at a suburban Milwaukee parts plant that makes catalytic converters. The plant supplies converters for almost all of GM's North American-built vehicles, as well as its Adam Opel AG unit in Germany.
A Ford Motor Co spokeswoman declined to discuss platinum and palladium supplies for the U.S. No. 2 automaker because of proprietary technology reasons.
"The only thing we can say is we're aware of the market situation and we're monitoring it," said the spokeswoman, Cheryl Eberwein.
A Chrysler Corp representative could not be reached for comment.
